claims.text: The awards are for talented early career scholars embarking on a university career.
The purpose of the award is to build a research team of sufficient scale to tackle a distinctive research problem.

Each grant runs over a period of 4 to 5 years.
Applicants must have had at least two years of full-time or equivalent experience in a research or teaching post after their PhD award.

Applicants must already hold a permanent academic appointment at a UK university at lecturer level or equivalent, or be nominated by a UK university that undertakes to offer a contract for the duration of the award.
Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK and be resident in the UK during the tenure of the award.
Applicants must be at an early stage of their academic career such that their research contribution trajectory has yet to become firmly established.
Applicants must not have held an equivalent award or fellowship that provided funds to establish an independent research group.
Applicants must not have held project grant funding in excess of £100k in a single award.
Applicants must not have led a team of research staff or managed PDRA staff.
Personal funding that exceeds £100k in a single award is allowable provided the award had no provision for managing staff.
Research Leadership Awards are tenable in UK universities with research degree awarding powers.
Applicants at Senior Lecturer, Reader/Associate Professor or Professor level or equivalent are not eligible to apply.
Proposals are welcome in any research area, with specific exceptions.
Research into studies of disease, illness and disabilities in humans and animals is not funded.
Research intended to inform clinical practice or the development of medical applications is not funded.
Policy-driven research where the principal objective is to assemble an evidence base for immediate policy initiatives is not funded.
Research where advocacy is an explicit component is not funded.
Research aimed principally at an immediate commercial application is not funded.
Proposals in which the balance between assembling a database and the related subsequent research is heavily inclined to the former are not funded.
At least 75% of the resources requested must be used to provide funding for staff costs.
Funding for staff costs can include teaching replacement for up to 24 months where the applicant holds a permanent appointment.
Funding for staff costs can include the applicant's salary up to a maximum of £250,000 (prorated) if they do not hold a permanent appointment.
The Trust expects the university to contribute any remaining salary costs for the applicant throughout the grant duration.
Salaries for research staff, including research assistants, research technicians, and postgraduate students, can be included.
The applicant is expected to dedicate a minimum of 0.8 FTE to the award.
Research assistants should have a research degree or equivalent research experience.
Tuition fees and maintenance costs for one or more PhD studentships may be included.
Support for an overseas student is allowable but requires explicit justification.
The additional costs of overseas student fees will need to be waived or covered by the institution.
There will be no provision for overhead costs.
Associated research costs can be included up to a maximum of 25% of the total budget.
Examples of eligible associated research costs include pool technical services, computing, clerical staff costs, and travel and subsistence costs directly related to the research activity.
Each institution is limited to one bid only.
Institutional approval by the host institution is required as part of the application procedure.
The host institution must confirm the necessary financial commitment and provide details of facilities.
The host department must have identified and secured the source of funding for an applicant by the closing date.
Funding contributed by the host university must be drawn from generally available funds and cannot be associated with any other grants.
Host universities should ensure the starting salary has been agreed with the applicant prior to finalising the application.
Host departments must provide the candidate with their own computer and dedicated desk and/or laboratory space.
Host departments must also provide the candidate with the necessary computing equipment for working from home, where applicable.
Once a university has selected its chosen candidate, it should send the applicant’s name, departmental affiliation, and email address to Vicky Marlow.
Access to the Leverhulme Trust Grants Management System will be granted after the candidate is selected.
Google Chrome is the recommended browser for the Grants Management System.
Applicants should refer to the Application Help Notes when completing the application form.

claims.text: UK universities can apply to establish a Leverhulme Research Centre for outstanding original research.
The research should aspire to achieve a step-change in scholarship.
The Centenary Research Centre round is expected to open in February 2027.
Outline applications are expected to be submitted in June 2027.
Universities of Oxford and Cambridge and Imperial College London are eligible to apply in this round.
The Trust aims to encourage new approaches that may establish or reshape a field of study.
The Trust aims to transform our understanding of a significant contemporary topic.
Up to £10 million is available for up to 10 years.
Eligible institutions are universities in the UK registered by the Office for Students and holding their own research degree awarding powers.
A Leverhulme Research Centre can be based at a single university or a collaboration between multiple institutions.
Collaborative research centres are encouraged.
Each UK university can submit one application as a principal applicant.
UK universities can act as a partner in multiple proposals led by other universities.
The participation of international institutions is encouraged but not required.
The Trust invites applications for Leverhulme Research Centres that will conduct research of outstanding originality.
The Trust encourages higher-risk, fundamental, curiosity-driven, and multi-disciplinary research.
The choice of research topic is open, with exceptions for ineligible areas like medical and clinical research.
The chosen topic should be large-scale enough to support an ambitious research agenda for up to ten years.
Leverhulme Research Centres should not duplicate existing activity at a comparable scale.
Funding is available for up to 10 years, with a mid-term review.
Proposed centres can require less than the maximum £10 million funding and a duration shorter than 10 years.
Funding requested should be proportionate to the centre’s proposed duration.
Research centres are encouraged to seek additional concurrent support from other funding bodies.
The Trust will not award follow-on funding.
At least 75% of resources must fund research staff.
Associated research costs can be included up to a maximum of 25% of the total budget.
Institutions hosting a centre must provide office and workspace.
The Trust does not make awards on a full economic costing basis.
Any increases in costs over the lifetime of the centres must be managed within the awarded funding.
Prospective applicants should follow their university’s internal selection process first.
Universities should contact Emily Nisbet at [email protected] with the name and email of their chosen applicant.
The chosen applicant will be given access to the Grants Management System to begin their outline application.
The June 2027 closing date is for the receipt of outline applications.
Invitations for full-stage applications are expected in September.
The deadline for full-stage applications is at the end of the year (of the invitation).
Applications must be submitted by a principal applicant based in a UK university who will act as Director.
Details of the proposed wider leadership team should be provided.
Applications are considered via a two-stage process: outline bid and detailed proposal.
The outline bid includes a short form and a five-page description of the centre’s structure and research activity.
The description should include reasons why the research is important, key research questions, and how the centre will contribute.
The description should detail the centre's structure, including single or multi-site, institutions involved, and key staff.
The description should justify the choice of principal applicant and senior staff.
The description should indicate how resources might be used over the centre’s duration.
Institutions hosting a centre will be required to provide all necessary office and workspace and any other appropriate university support.
Following shortlisting of outline bids, those selected will be invited to submit a detailed proposal.
A statement of support from the applying institution is required for the detailed proposal.
Those whose full applications are shortlisted will be invited to interview.
Final decisions are anticipated to be made by the Trust Board at its subsequent board meeting.
The Trust is unable to provide feedback on applications.
